clue.text: Eric gets doctor in real trouble

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the reworked word, so 'in' marks a container
real in trouble is real thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor

explanation.surface: A man named Eric has called a doctor because he is in real difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare first name defines by example: Eric Ambler wrote spy thrillers. 'trouble' gives ALER, which 'in' splits around the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was a British thriller writer, so his first name stands for the surname by example.

clue.text: Acted as go-between, taking time and thought

indicators.note: a word taking another in holds it, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: to act as go-between between parties is to mediate

explanation.surface: A negotiator who mediated a dispute did so slowly and thoughtfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditated means pondered or reflected, a past-tense synonym of thought.

clue.text: Oriental sailor, a rogue changing sides

indicators.note: changing one letter for another, the R for the L, is a substitution
the sides are right and left, R and L, which swap places in the word

parts.note: a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: An Eastern seaman is described as a scoundrel who has defected to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' swaps R (right) and L (left) in RASCAL, giving LASCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia, historically serving on European ships.

clue.text: Leading Republicans' euphemism naively downplaying illegal torture in other nations

definitions.text: Leading Republicans' euphemism naively downplaying illegal torture in other nations

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken, the first letter of each in turn

parts.words: Republicans' euphemism naively downplaying illegal torture in other nations

explanation.surface: A political jibe at Republican leaders who use soft language to play down torture done abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes extraordinary rendition, the US practice of sending suspects abroad for interrogation and torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary rendition is the euphemism for transferring prisoners to other countries where torture may be used.

clue.text: Homes & Gardens, perhaps, allows one to escape from life as it is

indicators.note: letting something escape from a word means taking it out

parts.note: life as it truly is is reality
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lifestyle magazine lets its readers escape from the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: Homes & Gardens is a magazine, which makes the definition look like a title; it means houses and land, real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is real estate, property such as homes and gardens, given here by example.

clue.text: Do this to an outcast

indicators.note: doing the answer's action to a word means writing it backwards, as the answer itself is a word turned round

parts.note: a leper is the proverbial outcast

explanation.surface: An instruction on how to treat a social pariah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do this to' asks you to apply the answer to LEPER: written backwards it gives the answer, and one also drives an outcast away.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive away, which is what society does to a leper or outcast.

clue.text: Singular Anglo-Saxon orientation

definitions.meaning: Angus Wilson's novel Anglo-Saxon ..., from Alice Through the Looking-Glass; the singular of its second word is wanted
one's stance or way of facing things, as of an aircraft or a mind

explanation.surface: A remark about a single Englishman's outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Orientation is synonym for position or stance, both literally (aircraft) and of opinion.

clue.text: Letter from the reserve

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer army reserve

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: US president died in house abroad

indicators.note: the letter for died goes inside the foreign house

parts.note: maison is French for house
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An American president passed away while living in a house overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States.

clue.text: Primate's alternative nomenclature

parts.note: the Primate of All England when this appeared was Archbishop Rowan Williams, and the tree called rowan has another name

explanation.surface: Something about a monkey's other name, or a bishop's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an ape, but it is an archbishop: Rowan Williams, so a rowan tree, whose other name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan tree is also commonly called by this two-word name, so it is an alternative name for rowan.

clue.text: Oil company turns over alternative for plant

indicators.note: the reversed company goes over, around, the other piece, so it is a container
turns means the company's letters are read the other way round

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
an alternative is an other

explanation.surface: An oil firm reverses its position and backs an alternative energy plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests an oil refinery in the surface, but it is a garden herb. 'turns' gives PB, which 'over' wraps round the alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is any plant whose leaves or stems are cooked as a vegetable or flavouring.

clue.text: Record comment of satisfied guest?

parts.note: an athlete's record is their fastest ever, while a happy guest might say they had the most enjoyable stay so far

explanation.surface: A remark a contented visitor writes in a hotel book.
explanation.definitionFit: A record performance is the fastest so far, and a pleased guest says they had the finest stay so far.

clue.text: Waves, being very often unseen

parts.note: radiation waves beyond the violet end of the spectrum, which the eye cannot see; very is a Latin prefix meaning beyond

explanation.surface: A remark about waves that usually go unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiation beyond visible violet light is invisible to the human eye, matching the waves described.

clue.text: Drinks for the young?

explanation.surface: Asking which drinks are suitable for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Tots are small drams of liquor and also small children, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Initial plan drifts aimlessly on drifter

indicators.note: in a down or across charade, on means placed after, so the drifter follows
drifts moved aimlessly loses its order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a raft drifts on the water, so it is a drifter

explanation.surface: A preliminary scheme wanders off course while sitting on a floating vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifter' looks like a fishing boat or a wanderer, but here it is a floating platform. 'aimlessly' gives FIRSTD, and 'on' puts the drifter after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A first draft is an initial version of a plan or document.

clue.text: People not having the right to quarters with the street as their resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged
not having something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Homeless people with no right to lodgings end up taking to the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes one R from QUARTERS, leaving QUATERS; add ST and 'resort' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Squatters are people occupying property without a legal right, matching the clue's people.

clue.text: Beads for starlets?

definitions.meaning: small convex mouldings in architecture, round a column
read as star-gals, with astra being Latin for stars and gals being girls

explanation.surface: Asking whether jewellery suits young actresses.
explanation.definitionFit: An astragal is a small convex bead moulding in classical architecture.

clue.text: Inside is where bird begins

parts.note: a chick starts its life within the hard casing laid by its mother

explanation.surface: A riddle about where a bird's life starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird develops inside the fragile outer casing of an egg before hatching.

clue.text: As a lodger, there's less than sufficient in it for classification as a native

definitions.note: native is used here as an adjective, like the answer

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in the lodger phrase, so in marks a container

parts.note: a lodger lives in digs, British slang for rented rooms

indicators.note: less than the full word means it is cut short

parts.note: sufficient means enough

explanation.surface: A lodger without enough of a stake cannot be classed as a true local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' drops the last two letters, giving ENOU, which 'in' places inside the lodger's IN DIGS. Digs is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous means native to a place, originating there naturally.

clue.text: A cat is of very little matter

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat doesn't count for much.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, a tiny amount of matter.

clue.text: It's preferable when dry to get in a drink

indicators.note: one piece gets in the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: beer is a drink
TT, teetotal, means dry, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: It's better to be dry than to get into drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Better and preferable are synonyms for more desirable.

clue.text: A 4 — pray the treatment may effect a cure

definitions.note: describes a remedy designed to cure, a noun sense like the answer

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, a rendition, is a version

indicators.note: pray the given treatment, worked over, has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Praying that some medical treatment will cure the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the answer of 4 down; RENDITION means VERSION. 'treatment' rearranges PRAY THE to THERAPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion therapy is a treatment intended to cure habits by linking them with unpleasant stimuli.

clue.text: She needs length and space

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A woman needs room and space.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's name, so it stands for a female, a she.

clue.text: Proprietor or new management

indicators.note: managing letters means arranging them, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business owner or the new management takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the proprietor of something.

clue.text: Live at home after a short break as an artist

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second in the clue, so the break precedes

parts.note: HOL is short for holiday, a break
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Being at home after a brief holiday as an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts BE IN after HOL, short for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was a German Renaissance painter at the court of Henry VIII.

clue.text: Get out, caught off a no-ball, perhaps

indicators.note: caught comes off, after, the extra, so it is placed at the end

parts.note: in cricket a no-ball adds a run to the batting side, an example of an extra
CT is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A batsman is out, caught off a no-ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket you can't be caught off a no-ball, so the surface is a joke; extras are runs not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to get or draw something out.

clue.text: Man with a line at 90°, first to last

indicators.note: the initial letter moves to the end

parts.note: a right angle is 90 degrees: R plus angle

explanation.surface: A man draws a line at a right angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 90° is a right angle, R ANGLE; 'first to last' moves the R to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with a rod and line, so is a man with a line.

clue.text: Poles without very foreign accent

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the poles wrap around

parts.note: S and S, the abbreviations for south and the poles
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: Poles lack a very foreign accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: S and S (poles, as south) around TRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is emphasis on a syllable, an accent in speech.
